title: Example State University — AI practice assessment (FICTIONAL)
note: FICTIONAL CONTENT for exercising printed output. Not a real assessment.

blocks.text: Executive summary

This report describes a fictional assessment of AI practice at Example State University. Every finding, citation, locator and figure below is invented for the purpose of exercising the printed output of the report template, and none of it describes any real institution. The assessment covered five areas across five operating units over a nine-week window. Of twenty-two assessed items, eight produced a supported finding, five produced a partial finding where the available evidence was consistent but incomplete, three produced a gap where an assessor looked and the practice was absent, and six remain unassessed because the fieldwork window closed before the relevant records could be opened. Unassessed items are reported as unassessed throughout and are excluded from every count of strengths and gaps; they are not scored, defaulted, or rolled into a proportion. Table 1 lists all twenty-two items and its dispositions sum to these figures.

The strongest single observation is that controls which are enforced by configuration survive staff turnover and controls which are enforced by convention do not. The clearest gap is that prompt and response logs generated by three applications carry no data classification and no retention setting, a condition that two separate active policies already address and neither of which is being executed against that log stream. The most consequential open question is whether prompt text submitted to an external vendor falls inside the institutional definition of institutional data; both readings are defensible from the policy text as written, and the answer changes the disposition of four items.
Finding F-001 — configuration-enforced review survives turnover

Across fourteen sampled changes in the sampled repository, every merge to the protected branch required a named human reviewer, enforced by a required status check rather than by team convention. The distinction matters more than it appears to. A convention is carried by the people who remember it, and the assessment observed two units where an equivalent convention had quietly stopped being followed after a role change, without anyone noticing and without any record being produced. A required check produces a record when it is removed. The unit that enforces review in configuration can therefore demonstrate what happened; the units that enforce it by convention can only describe what they believe happens.

The limitation on this finding is that it establishes the presence of a gate, not the quality of the review passing through it. Fourteen changes is a sample, the sample was drawn from a single repository, and no attempt was made to assess whether the named reviewers read the changes carefully. A gate that everyone approves without reading is still a gate, and this assessment cannot distinguish the two cases from the records available to it.

blocks.text: Finding F-002 — AI prompt and response logs are unclassified and unretained

Three applications write prompt text and model responses into the default application log store. The assessor examined the retention configuration for that store and found it set to indefinite. The assessor then requested the data classification assigned to the store and was told that none has been assigned and that no steward is recorded. Two separate active standards reach this condition. One requires a defined retention period for application logs; the other requires a classification and a named steward for institutional data. Neither is a draft and neither is ambiguous about whether it applies to an application log store.

The instinct on seeing a finding of this shape is to write a new policy. A new policy would not have changed this condition, because two existing policies already say the right thing. What is missing is execution against a log stream that did not exist when either policy was written. The corrective action indicated by the evidence is an assignment of ownership for that stream, not a further statement of principle.

blocks.text: Finding F-003 - interview assertion is not corroborated by any record

Service desk staff state that an AI-generated ticket summary is always read against the original thread before the ticket is routed. The assessor has no reason to doubt the statement and no way to confirm it. The ticketing system records the routing decision and the time it was made; it does not record whether the summary or the thread was the basis for it. An assertion of this kind is recorded here as an assertion and is counted as neither a strength nor a gap, because promoting it to implementation evidence would mean reporting a belief as an observation.

The practical consequence is narrow and worth stating plainly. If the University wishes this practice to be demonstrable rather than merely stated, the change required is to the ticketing record, not to the practice. One additional captured field would move this item from an assertion to a directly inspectable artifact, and that is a smaller piece of work than it appears.

blocks.text: Phase 1 — first ninety days
Assign ownership for the AI prompt and response log stream

The finding at F-002 is an ownership gap rather than a policy gap. The action indicated by the evidence is to name a steward for the log store and to apply one of the two retention schedules already in force. This is the only item in the roadmap whose prerequisite is a decision rather than work.
Answer the institutional-data scope question

Four assessed items are blocked on whether prompt text submitted to an external vendor is institutional data. Until that question has an answer, the disposition of those items cannot honestly be set, and any remediation designed against a guess may be designed against the wrong reading.
Phase 2 — ninety to one hundred and eighty days
Extend configuration-enforced review beyond the one unit that has it

Finding F-001 established that a configuration-enforced gate produces a record when it is removed and a convention does not. Extending the enforced gate to the units currently relying on convention is the action with the clearest evidentiary support in this report.
Close the six unassessed items
Six items remain unassessed because the fieldwork window closed. They are not gaps and they are not passes. Closing them is ordinary remaining work and should not be confused with remediation.
Phase 3 — beyond one hundred and eighty days
Give the model-change watch practice a named owner

The practice observed at ITM-009 is real, documented and repeated, and it exists because two engineers decided it should. It has no policy behind it and no role accountable for it. The risk is continuity, not compliance, and the action is an assignment rather than a control.
